text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.66% today after oil prices dropped sharply over the weekend. Crude fell for the second consecutive day as markets grew hopeful about a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict, reducing fears of major supply disruptions. The stock had climbed steeply earlier in the week (up about 2.7% from Tuesday to Thursday) as geopolitical tensions pushed oil higher, so today's decline reverses some of those recent gains.

There's also an undercurrent of political uncertainty weighing on the sector. News coverage of the midterm elections raised questions about what a Democratic-controlled Congress could mean for energy policy — including potential shifts toward renewables and away from traditional oil and gas — adding to the pressure alongside the retreat in oil prices themselves.
